entries.text: **Drink potions and open doors without leaving form** → Feral stays in form instead of paying mana to shift back.
**Keep upgrading your weapon as Feral** → weapons matter in forms now.
**Tauren: War Stomp in bear form** → racials work while shapeshifted (90-second cooldown).
**Revive** at 12, **Nature's Grasp** at 10, **Omen of Clarity** baseline at 20.
In forms, your auto-attack uses your **weapon's DPS**, and weapon enchants and procs work.
Most **potions and consumables work in forms**, and most doors and objects too.
New signatures: Berserk (Feral, 31), Wild Growth (Restoration, 31), Eclipse (Balance).
Tiger's Fury is gone (replaced by **Shifting Power**), and **Primal Bite** replaces Mangle.
**Barkskin without leaving form** → it works while shapeshifted now.
**Root indoors too** → Entangling Roots works inside buildings and caves now.
Druids went 12–14 vs other classes in the beta tournament finals; Minpojke finished top 6.
**Drop a Frost Trap mid-fight and back off** → traps work in combat now, so you can fix a bad pull without running first.
**Tame for the family ability, not the look** → Boar Charge, Spider Web, Turtle Shell Shield and Wolf Furious Howl each solve a different problem.
**Upgrade your own gear before your pet's food** → pets scale with your gear, so every upgrade counts twice.
**Aimed Shot** is baseline at 20 for every Hunter.
**Lone Wolf** (Marksmanship): 20% more damage with no pet out.
Pets scale with your gear, and every pet family has its own unique ability. Foxes are a new family.
Survival is a real melee spec now, with Strider Kick and Lacerating Strikes.
Traps work **in combat**, and all traps share one 30-second cooldown.
**Play group PvP from max range** → hunters went 7–11 in beta finals duels, but range is your edge in battlegrounds.
**Scatter Shot an Undead when you need them locked down** → they can't use Will of the Forsaken while Scatter Shotted.
**Frost Nova, then Ice Lance** → Ice Lance hits frozen targets for big damage.
**Learn Comprehension, the new minor tradeskill** → you can read the scrolls monsters drop.
**Plan smaller pulls than the old AoE kites** → Cone of Cold is shorter, so huge kite-pulls are riskier.
**Frostfire Bolt** at 40 counts as both Fire and Frost.
Arcane: **Arcane Blast** (11) and the new **Arcane Wrath** (16). Missile Barrage is now an early talent.
Cone of Cold lasts less time, to stop huge kite-pulls. Orc Mages are new.
Fire: **Heating Up** is Forever's Hot Streak; crits shorten your next Pyroblast.
Frost: **Ice Lance** (11) does 300% more to Frozen targets, on an 8-second cooldown shared with Fire Blast; **Fingers of Frost** makes targets count as Frozen.
**Root first, then Ice Lance on Fingers of Frost** → that combo is your burst window.
**Undead Mages: hold Will of the Forsaken for Warlock fears** → that's the fight you'll see most.
Mages went 4–12 vs other classes in the beta tournament finals, and all four lost in the same round.
**Bind Holy Strike as soon as you get it at 6** → you finally have a real button to press, not just auto-attack.
**Judge on cooldown** → Judgement no longer eats your Seal, so there's no reason to save it.
**Run Seal of Fury while soloing, not just tanking** → its absorb shield means fewer stops between pulls.
**Holy Strike** at 6 and **Consecration** for everyone at 20.
**Judgement no longer consumes your Seal.**
**Seal of Fury** at 10: the tanking seal. Hits add Holy damage and an absorb shield; its Judgement taunts.
Salvation and Mass Salvation are gone. Lay on Hands is a 20-minute cooldown.
Seal twisting now comes from the Ret talent **Twist of Light**, not baseline.
**Save Will of the Forsaken (Undead) for a Fear, Charm or Sleep** → breaking a Warlock's Fear is the trade that wins duels.
**Try a shockadin build if you want burst** → Holy Shock is a 21-point talent on a 10-second cooldown now.
Paladins went 16–13 vs other classes in the beta tournament finals, with four undefeated qualifiers.
**Fade the moment a dungeon pull turns on you** → its threat drop is doubled now.
**Level as Shadow and stay in Shadowform** → Shadow spells cost half the mana, so you drink far less.
**Stack Renews with other Priests** → Renew from several Priests can sit on one target now.
**Divine Spirit** baseline at 30 and **Shadow Word: Death** at 32 (costs you 30% of your max health if it doesn't kill).
**Fear Ward** and **Devouring Plague** for every Priest at 20, whatever your race.
New signatures: Penance (Discipline), Prayer of Mending (Holy), Vampiric Embrace (Shadow, 16).
Shadowform halves Shadow spell mana costs and doubles their crit bonus.
Undead get **Dark Sacrifice** at 20: turn health into mana over time.
**Fear Ward yourself before engaging a Warlock** → every Priest has it now, and Warlocks won the beta tournament.
**Only Shadow Word: Death when it will kill** → it's an instant finisher, but it costs you if they live.
Priests went 9–12 vs other classes in the beta tournament finals.
**Don't pass on a good axe** → Hack and Slash gives axes a chance at an extra attack, like swords.
**Run poisons and a Sharpening Stone together** → they stack now, so it's free damage.
**Sap and sneak past packs you don't need** → you skip fights that give little XP and keep moving.
**Sap no longer breaks Stealth.**
Distract also lowers nearby enemies' stealth detection for 10 seconds.
New signatures: **Mutilate** and **Venom** (Assassination), **Thousand Cuts** (Subtlety).
Poisons get more charges and **stack with Sharpening Stones** and other temporary enchants.
Rogues can use **one-handed axes**. Hack and Slash replaces the old weapon specializations.
**Sap the healer, then stay stealthed** → you pick the fight and the target.
**Use Distract only when you're ready to commit** → it lowers stealth detection but tells nearby players a Rogue is around.
Rogues went 5–11 vs other classes in the beta tournament finals.
**Imbue your weapon once when you log in** → imbues last an hour now, not 5 minutes.
**Pair Rockbiter with Spirit Weapons as Enhancement** → you can off-tank small groups.
**Set up a Call of the Elements preset at 20** → one cast drops all four totems.
**Call of the Elements** at 20: preset four totems and drop them all in one 3-second cast.
**Totemic Call** (was Totemic Projection) pulls all your totems to you, on a 30-second cooldown.

Lava Burst was cut before launch: **Call of Thunder** (+5% crit on Lightning Bolt and Chain Lightning) takes its spot, and Elemental Mastery is now **Lightning Mastery**. Also new: Maelstrom Weapon (Enhancement), Riptide (Restoration, healing over time only, 12-second cooldown).
Totems: 1-second global cooldown, and buff totems last 5 minutes.
Weapon imbues last **60 minutes** and stack with stones and oils. Windfury Totem is a party buff.
**Pull your totems to you with Totemic Call mid-fight** → keep them on the fight instead of re-dropping them (30-second cooldown).
**Take Earthbound (Elemental, 16)** → Earthbind Totem roots nearby enemies for 5 seconds.
Shamans went 19–11 vs other classes in the beta tournament finals and took 3rd and 4th.
**Finish low targets with Drain Soul** → the kill gives you a Soul Shard; damage ticks alone rarely do since launch tuning.
**Grab your free mount at 40 from Strahad Farsan in Ratchet** → save the gold for training and gear.
**Stack some Spirit** → Life Tap scales with it, so you sit to drink less.
**Pets scale with your stats**, but launch tuning cut pet health to 2 per point of your Stamina (was 7.5). A Nov 6 hotfix gave the Voidwalker about 40 more base health.
**Soul Link** is a 21-point talent; **Demonic Pact** (31) keeps Demonic Sacrifice when you swap pets.
Curse of Agony and Curse of Doom are now **Banes**: one Bane per Warlock per target.
Firestone and Spellstone are weapon imbues that stack with Wizard Oil.
New signatures: Wrack (Affliction, 31), Bane of Havoc (21) and Incinerate (31) in Destruction.
**Plan your fight around Fear getting answered** → Undead Will of the Forsaken it and every Priest has Fear Ward, so don't open with it.
Warlocks went 26–7 vs other classes in the beta tournament finals and took 1st and 2nd. That was level-30 dueling; at 60, more trinkets and Fear answers will change things.
**Charge in Battle Stance, then swap to whatever the fight needs** → Tactical Mastery keeps 10 Rage, so swapping no longer resets you.
**Keep Rend and Thunder Clap in your rotation** → both scale with Attack Power now, so they get better as your gear does.
**Victory Rush right after every kill** → a free 10% heal each fight, so you stop to eat far less.
**Tactical Mastery** is baseline at 14: keep 10 Rage when you swap stances.
**Victory Rush** at 20: after a kill, an instant hit that heals 10% of your max health.
Bloodthirst no longer heals. It gives 10% movement speed instead.
Rage from hits ignores armor and shields, and crits give 75% more Rage.
Thunder Clap works in Defensive Stance; Rend and Thunder Clap now scale with Attack Power.
**Hunt mounted players with Spearing Strike (Arms)** → it dismounts them and hits for double damage on riders.
**Queue battlegrounds with a healer on your hip** → in the level-30 beta duels, warriors struggled against kiting classes on their own.
**Click every flight master you pass** → long flights only work once you've unlocked the stops in between.
**Do "The Great Outdoors" around level 5** → camping and campfire buffs.
**Pick two gathering professions, like Herbalism and Mining** → they pay for your level-40 mount, about 100 gold.
**Take the starter profession quest** → it hands you Mining, Skinning or Herbalism plus 2 free skill points, a head start on your mount gold.
**Visit your class trainer every couple of levels** → new spells are easy to miss.
**Group with strangers hunting the same mobs** → only the first group to tag gets credit, so groups level faster than solo racers.
**Invite your friends before you leave the starting area** → groups land on the same layer, so you can actually see each other.
**Learn First Aid in your first few levels** → bandages from the cloth you're already looting cut your downtime between pulls, on any class.
**Pre-install tonight from the Battle.net game version menu** → you're not stuck downloading at 5 PM.
**Set your hearthstone at a hub, take every flight path, and learn Cooking** → faster travel and campfires from day one.
**Mages** went 4–12 on finals day, after a week of forum calls to nerf them. Hype isn't results.
**Pick your class for fun first.** No arena is announced; Forever PvP is battlegrounds and world PvP.
**Shamans** were the other standout: 19–11 and both 3rd and 4th place.
**Warlocks:** 26–7 in duels vs other classes. Soul Link at 21 points plus pet scaling made them hard to kill at 30. Launch tuning cut pet health to 2 per point of Stamina (was 7.5).
**Who:** 36 finalists, top 4 of each class after six Swiss rounds with 1,380 players.
**Why it may not hold at 60:** more trinkets and Fear answers, damage outscaling healing, and BGs where nobody is forced to stand and duel.
**Lost?** Ask any guard: it marks the bank, trainers and more on your map.
**No mount until 40.** Budget about 100g for Apprentice Riding plus your first mount. Skip trainer ranks you won't use to save up.
**Other continents:** zeppelins and boats only, unless a Mage or Warlock helps.
**Shamans and Druids** are the only classes with a travel form before 40.
**Travel order:** hearthstone > Mage portal / Warlock summon > flight path > zeppelin. No modern-style portal rooms.
**Chase the Hyjal Summit legendary** → the 20-player raid drops Forever's first legendary weapon.
**Get Honored with your home faction** → 10% off riding and mounts. Add the Bartering Legacy talent for up to another 10% off mounts.
**Have an Alchemist and an Herbalist in your group** → steady potions are what win early raids.
**Play Warlock or Horde Paladin for a free mount** → Warlocks get a level-40 quest from Strahad Farsan in Ratchet, and Horde Paladins have their own.
**Save 1,000 gold by 60** → that's Journeyman Riding, and epic mounts are 200 gold each.
**Use camp buffs to cover missing classes** → they don't stack with matching class buffs, but they fill gaps.
**Camp with friends** → each player adds one item, so a group fire stacks more buffs.
**Do "The Great Outdoors" around level 5 and learn Cooking** → you unlock campfires, the base for every camp buff.
**Eat Well Fed food before a grind** → +5% kill XP for about 15 minutes.
**Grab a Leatherworking Camp Tent** → a 1-hour rested-XP buff that survives death.
**Level Cooking to 90, then 200** → your campfire holds 5, then 10 camp items instead of 3.
**Log out on a Cozy Sleeping Bag** → it counts as a rested area, so you earn rested XP while offline, which doubles your kill XP when you're back.
**Aim for rank 2 first** → that's the PvP trinket. Later ranks unlock cloaks (3), a necklace (4), mounts (11) and epic weapons (14).
**Hold bases, then carry the center flag to one you own** → the four bases earn steady points, the flag scores bonus points, and first to 2,000 wins.
**Play a few games every week instead of marathons** → Rank Points have a weekly cap, so consistency beats grinding. Weekly tasks add bonus Honor, Rank Points and Legacy Points.
**Play whichever battleground you enjoy** → Honor is normalized across battlegrounds, so there's no penalty for skipping Alterac Valley.
**Queue from the Darkspear Raiders base at Merchant Coast** → there's a portal straight into Darkspear Islands. Battlemasters in the capitals and the Barrens work too.
**Turn in Marks of Honor for Darkspear reputation** → it unlocks vendor trinkets, rings, cloaks, weapons and armor, and Exalted opens a tabard questline.
**Buy your mount from Genn Fairweather on Zephras Isle** → Galestriders are sold there, at Fairweather Stables.
**Get the Skyborne Heroic Pack or higher** → it's required to play the race.
**Pick Skyborne for a mobile character** → Wind Blessed gives 2% haste, Walk on Air is on a 90-second cooldown, and Skysight and Read Leyline can be cast while moving.
**Roll Skyborne on Horde if you want Shaman** → Horde Skyborne work with the Earthen Ring, which unlocks Shaman for them.
**Try a Skyborne Druid** → you get druid forms built just for the race.
**Bring one tank, one healer and three damage dealers, and talk before you pull** → a 10-second plan beats a 10-minute run back from the graveyard.
**Camp a night at Krol'dok Stronghold (40–55)** → it's outdoors, it changes at night when the cultists start chanting, and the wide level range keeps it useful for a long time.
**Farm Blackmaw Hold and Shaper's Terrace at 55–60** → they're your best gear sources before Dec 9 raids.
**Go see Alcaz Prison (48–53)** → it's enterable for the first time ever, Defias against naga, in the prison where King Varian was said to be held.
**Group with people within a few levels of you** → higher-level members reduce everyone's kill XP.
**Travel to Hall of Thanes as a group** → Horde have to sneak in under Ironforge, through Alliance territory.
**Explore Shen'dralas** → the ruins between Mulgore and Desolace are finally open, with links into Maraudon and Razorfen Downs.
**Head to Riverglades around 35** → 150+ new quests on the Eastern Kingdoms coast and the outdoor dungeon Krol'dok Stronghold, so you skip the classic mid-level slump.
**Level a Skyborne on Zephras Isle (1–12)** → a whole starting story of Highborne exiles and wind spirits before you reach the main continents.
**Set up camp in Mount Hyjal at 60** → it holds Darkwhisper Gorge, the Hyjal Summit raid, and an entrance to Barrow Deeps, so it'll be your endgame home.
**Be online at 3 PM Central on Oct 27** → the best names go first, and it's first come, first served. The bot posts a heads-up 30 minutes before.
**If a first name is taken, change the surname, not the spelling** → names are first + last and unique per region, and "Grommash Ashfall" ages better than "Grommashh."
**Reserve on the account you'll actually play** → the reservation is tied to the Battle.net account that bought the Skyborne pack.
**Spend your 3 names on launch characters** → the 3 are shared across all rulesets, so two PvP names leaves just one for Normal or Roleplay.
**Use one surname across your roster** → only the full name has to be unique, so a shared "family name" is easy to claim and makes your alts recognizable.
**Don't count on a transfer to fix a mistake** → there's no cross-ruleset grouping and no character transfers at launch, so double-check the ruleset at character creation.
**If a friend "vanishes" in a busy city, invite them** → the world is split into layers when crowded, and grouping pulls you onto the same one.
**Level an alt on Normal or Roleplay guilt-free** → collections and Legacy points are shared across rulesets (except Hardcore), so that time still powers up your PvP account.

**Locked out of a faction on PvP? Try again later instead of rerolling** → Blizzard recalculates the balance through the day, and the lock only ever blocks new characters, never ones you already have.
**Treat Hardcore as a free second shot when it arrives** → a Hardcore character that dies can transfer to another ruleset, PvP included, so a death isn't the end of that character.
**Add items:** every profession crafts three camp items. Each character can place one per camp (then waits an hour), and anyone can add to the same fire.
**Cozy Sleeping Bag:** earned through a quest chain across both continents. It stacks with camp buffs, and you can eat cooked food on it for even more XP.
**Get the buff:** sit within range for at least a minute. Buffs from different items combine into one Camp Benefits buff.
**Light a fire:** Cooking plus Flint and Tinder and wood. Basic Campfire (Cooking 1, 3 items) · Journeyman (Cooking 140, 5 items) · Expert (Cooking 220, 10 items). Each burns for about 10 minutes.

**What they do:** stat buffs a bit weaker than class buffs (they don't stack with them), plus utility: the Leatherworking Camp Tent gives rested XP, Engineering bots sell reagents and repair, and Herbalism and Mining can grow nodes.
**Alchemy + Herbalism** is the classic gold-making pair.
**Discounts:** Honored with your home faction saves 10% on riding and mounts.
**Gathering pays:** Herbalism, Mining and Skinning sell steadily early on.
**Target:** about 100g by 40 for your first mount, 1,000g by 60 for Journeyman Riding.
**Hardcore:** points earned there count everywhere, but not the other way around. PvP challenges are swapped for Hardcore-only ones.
**Rewards:** points also unlock account-wide cosmetics. At launch: a Replica Ironforge Air Rifle toy, a Spectral Bear Cub pet, a Spectral Bear Tabard and the Reins of the Spectral Bear mount.
**Spending:** each character can spend up to 16 points at launch across three trees: Professions, Adventure and Resourcefulness.
**Unlock:** your first point, usually at level 25. 150 in a crafting profession or exploring the entire world map also counts. Open it with **Y**.
**What it is:** Forever's replacement for achievements. 65 challenges, each worth one Legacy Point, earned across your whole Battle.net account.
**Where points come from:** Classes 27 (levels 25, 45 and 60 on all nine) · Tradeskills 18 · PvP 12 · Dungeons 3 · Raids 3 · Adventure 2.
**Dungeons:** kill XP inside dungeons went up 50% on Nov 8, so repeat runs pay better than they did at launch.
entries.source: Kaivax blue post, Dungeon Enemy XP Increased - Nov 8 (via timesaver.gg server-status; Wowhead and MMO-Champion blue trackers)

entries.text: **Explore:** new areas give a little XP.
**Gray quests and mobs** (5+ levels below) give no XP; quests over 5 levels below lose 10–20% per level.
**Grouping:** big parties split kill XP; quest turn-ins are never reduced.
**Rested XP** doubles kill XP. Log out in inns, cities or on a Cozy Sleeping Bag.
**Well Fed** food adds +5% kill XP; the Camp Tent adds a rested buff that survives death.
**Caps:** Apprentice 75 · Journeyman 150 (lvl 10) · Expert 225 (lvl 20) · Artisan 300 (lvl 35).
**New UI:** a profession window (K), recipe search and tracking, and a separate reagent bag slot.
**No passive bonuses.** Value comes from crafts and camp items, which unlock at skill 20, 140 and 300.
**Pairs:** Alch + Herb, BS + Mining, Eng + Mining (PvP), Ench + Tailoring, LW + Skinning.
**Tauren Cultivation** lets you pick herbs without Herbalism, or doubles yield with it.
**Two primaries** plus all three secondaries (Cooking, First Aid, Fishing). Secondaries can't be unlearned.
**Darkspear Islands:** bases first, then flag to a base you own. First to 2,000.
**Honor** buys blue and epic PvP sets; it's normalized across BGs, and holiday-week BGs give extra.
**Rank Points** have a weekly cap, so steady play beats marathons. Ranks reset each season.
**Weekly tasks** give bonus Honor, Rank Points, and sometimes a Legacy Point.
**Barrow Deeps** has three entrances: Mount Hyjal, Winterspring and Blackmaw Hold. Use whichever is closest to your group.
**Bosses in the client:** Barrow Deeps has 8 (including the Deepscar Matriarch and Sonya Darkhallow); Hyjal Summit has 13 (including the Ancient of Decay, the Council of Thorns and the Wild King).
**Hyjal Summit** is set after Archimonde's defeat and drops Forever's first legendary weapon.
**Legacy Points:** clearing Onyxia, all 13 Hyjal Summit bosses and all 8 Barrow Deeps bosses each earn one.
**Onyxia's Lair** keeps its classic attunement: the **Drakefire Amulet** quest chain. Start it before raid night, not on it.
**Three raids open Dec 9:** Barrow Deeps (10 players), Hyjal Summit (20) and the returning Onyxia's Lair (40).
**Epic at 60:** 1,000g Journeyman Riding, 200g per epic mount, +100% speed.
**Free mounts:** Warlocks via Strahad Farsan in Ratchet; Horde Paladins have their own quest.
**Horde vendors:** wolves in Orgrimmar, raptors in Sen'jin, kodos in Bloodhoof, skeletal horses in Brill.
**Mount at 40:** 100g for Apprentice Riding with your first mount; extra colors 20g.
17 of the 36 Forever Open finalists were Undead. Will of the Forsaken vs. Fear was huge.
Cannibalize restores mana as well as health in Forever.
In Darkspear Islands, the Horde fights alongside the Darkspear trolls; the Alliance shows up as the Theramore Expeditionary Force.
Orc Command is back: +5% pet damage for Hunters and Warlocks. Blood Fury is on a 2-minute cooldown.
Tauren Plainsrunning lost its mounted speed in the final pass, but now builds to +60% on foot.
Troll Berserking now lasts 15 seconds, up from 10.
Undead Touch of the Grave now has a 15-second internal cooldown, down from 25.
Will of the Forsaken breaks Charm, Fear and Sleep, but it no longer leaves you immune afterward.
Campfires can't hurt you below level 5. Blizzard changed that during the beta.
Choose Classic Mode on first launch and transmog turns off automatically. You still collect appearances.
Dalaran sat sealed under a violet dome for the entire original game. Forever finally lets you inside, through the sewers.
Dual specialization unlocks at level 40, the same level as your first mount.
entries.source: Blizzard class deep dive Oct 7 via https://kami-labs.fr/en/wow-forever/wow-forever-niveau-40-monture-double-specialisation/ ; https://buyboost.com/news/wow-forever/wow-forever-dual-spec

entries.text: Every race in Forever has two active and two passive racial abilities.
Exploring the entire world map earns a Legacy Point.
Forever is set before Molten Core opened, which is why the original raids are still locked.
Forever replaces achievements with the Legacy System: 65 challenges, each worth one account-wide point.
Forever's level cap is a permanent 60. New updates add zones, dungeons and raids instead of levels.
Gold is tight early. In the beta, three PC Gamer writers earned about 2.5 gold together in their first two hours.
In the original game, King Varian Wrynn was missing for years. In Forever, you'll find him as a prisoner in the new Alcaz Prison dungeon.
Mount Hyjal was blocked off in the original game. Players spent years sneaking in through map exploits just to look around. In Forever, it's the endgame zone.
Original 2004 WoW launched with zero battlegrounds. Forever launches with a brand-new 15v15 one.
Original WoW launched on Nov 23, 2004. Forever launches on Nov 4, 2026, almost 22 years later.
Shen'dralas is a new zone between Mulgore and Desolace, with dozens of new quests.
Skyborne start on Zephras Isle in Skywall, one of the elemental planes.
The Drowned City has no door: you dive underwater off the Stranglethorn coast, west of Grom'gol, to find it.
There are no flying mounts and no level scaling. Zones stay as dangerous as they were built.
Undead Paladins and Dwarf Shamans are playable. In 2004, those classes belonged only to the other faction.
You can collect high-level appearances early, but you can't wear them as transmog until level 60.
You can earn Legacy Points without ever fighting: maxing crafting professions and exploring the whole world map both count.
Your regular WoW subscription already includes Forever. No separate purchase.
A Hardcore character who dies can transfer to another ruleset, even PvP.
About 20 zombie plague spells turned up in the game files on Oct 30. Blizzard hasn't announced an event.
Advanced Leatherworking recipes need a Tanning Rack, the Leatherworker's tier 2 camp item.
All four Mage finalists in the Forever Open lost in the same round and split the Mage prize, about $1,389 each.
Alliance Skyborne are the High Order. Horde Skyborne are the Windshapers.
Barrow Deeps has three entrances: Mount Hyjal, Winterspring and Blackmaw Hold.
Barrow Deeps, once Illidan's prison, has 8 bosses. Names in the client include the Deepscar Matriarch and Sonya Darkhallow.
Battle Shout, Trueshot Aura and the Shaman buff totems all reach the whole raid in Forever.
Battlegrounds are shared across rulesets, except Hardcore.
Blackmaw Hold is a furbolg city hidden behind a sealed gate in Azshara, and the path inside may lead even deeper.
Blizzard aims for an ordinary monster to take a solo player about 10 to 15 seconds to kill.
Blizzard batches Forever's class balance changes on Tuesdays. The first round, Nov 10, covers Hunter and Warlock pets, Affliction and Enhancement.
entries.source: Kaivax, Class Tuning Incoming - November 10 (us forums thread 2404092) via https://timesaver.gg/blog/wow-forever-class-changes-november-10
entries.note: Re-check after the Nov 10 hotfixes; replace with what actually changed.

entries.text: Blizzard built a dueling arena in Hyjal Crater for Forever Open finals day, even though it was a community event.
Blizzard dev Aggrend said the beta found more problems in six hours than six months of internal testing.
Camp items come in three tiers per profession, at skill 20, 140 and 300.
Cooks can upgrade campfires to hold 5 or 10 camp items.
Dalaran's dungeon has several paths, so each group picks its own route through the city.
Dalaran's starting quest depends on your faction: Southshore for Alliance, Tarren Mill for Horde. Those two towns were the site of a famous world PvP rivalry in the original game.
Darkspear Islands is for levels 30–60, and the first team to 2,000 points wins.
Darkspear Islands mixes Eye of the Storm's neutral flag with Arathi Basin–style capture points.
Divine Spirit, Blessing of Kings and Improved Mark of the Wild are baseline in Forever. No talent points needed.
Dwarves deal +5% damage to beasts, and Undead get a chance to drain health. Racials got a pass.
Dwarves lost their crit racial in the final pass and got +1% hit instead.
Each profession's top camp item is a full workstation, like the Fishing Hut or the Master Forge.
Each side of Darkspear Islands has its own reputation: the Darkspear Raiders and the Theramore Expeditionary Force.
Engineers can make a Stealthman 52 that lets any class stealth out of combat on a cooldown.
First Aid's top camp item is a Plague Doctor's Laboratory.
Forever adds over 600 new recipes, mostly using materials from the original game.
Forever's 9 new dungeons span levels 13 to 60, so there's a new one to try at almost every stage of leveling.
Forever's Hyjal is set after Archimonde's defeat, unlike the Burning Crusade raid that replays the battle.
Forever's first new legendary is Taldramir, the Whispering Wood, a two-handed staff revealed an hour before launch.
Four days after launch, Blizzard raised kill XP in dungeons by 50% so repeat runs feel worth it.
entries.source: https://timesaver.gg/tools/wow-forever/server-status (Kaivax blue post, Dungeon Enemy XP Increased - Nov 8; also Wowhead/MMO-Champion blue trackers)

entries.text: Gnome Engineers have a racial that makes their gadgets backfire less.
Green monsters give less XP in Forever than in Classic. Blizzard says it balances the new food and camp buffs.
Hall of Thanes is the tomb of Ironforge's dwarven kings, and Dark Iron intruders have broken in.
Hemet Nesingwary's Stranglethorn quests add a Master Hunter's Spellsword option for casters.
Humans' Spirit racial doubled from 5% to 10% in the final racial pass.
Hunters must stand still for half a second before Auto Shot fires. Wands work the same way.
Hyjal Summit is a 20-player raid where Archimonde fell, and it drops Forever's first legendary weapon.
Hyjal Summit's 13 bosses include the Ancient of Decay, the Council of Thorns and the Wild King, per names in the client.
Ice Lance has an 8-second cooldown shared with Fire Blast, and Frost Blast is gone.
Krol'dok Stronghold's ogres kidnap travelers on the road, and the chanting only starts after dark.
Launch ships with nine new dungeons and over 1,000 new quests across 1–60.
Lava Burst was cut right before launch. Call of Thunder (+5% crit on Lightning Bolt and Chain Lightning) took its spot, and Elemental Mastery became Lightning Mastery.
Legacy Points are shared account-wide across rulesets, except Hardcore.
Mages get a new Arcane Wrath talent that adds spell power equal to 5% of max mana.
Mages have their own minor tradeskill, Comprehension, for reading scrolls that monsters drop.
New crafting materials include Azerothium Bar, Legionite Bar and Torbernite.
On the beta map, Riverglades' faction hubs are Rog'mar (Horde) and Farholde Keep (Alliance), held by the Brotherhood of the Horse.
One of the account-wide Legacy rewards is a mount: the Reins of the Spectral Bear.
Onyxia's Lair returns as a 40-player raid on Dec 9, with the classic Drakefire Amulet attunement.
Paladins get Holy Strike at level 6 and baseline Consecration at 20, and Judgement no longer eats your Seal.
Paladins get a new seal built for tanking, plus some group-healing talents.
Paladins learn Righteous Fury at level 10, down from 16.
Paladins still have no interrupt and no slow in Forever. Blizzard kept that weakness on purpose.
Profession titles come from the Azeroth Commerce Authority (Alliance) and Durotar Supply and Logistics (Horde).
PvP Rank 1 takes 750 Rank Points. Rank 14 takes 24,750.
PvP Rank 11 unlocks mounts, and Rank 14 unlocks epic weapons.
Raid tier sets for all nine classes turned up in the game files in September, each with alternate colors.
Rank Points have a weekly cap. No more account-sharing to keep a rank.
Reaching 60 takes 4,084,700 XP, the same total as Classic.
Riverglades has the Bloodmaster's Ring, where you fight ogre brawlers.
Riverglades is a 35–45 zone about everyday frontier life rather than world-ending stakes.
Shaman totems now last 5 minutes, and weapon imbues last an hour.
Shamans get three PvP gear sets in Forever: healer, melee and caster.
Shaper's Terrace is a titan facility in Un'Goro, and its consoles run on power crystals you gather in the crater.
Six race and class combos are new: Gnome Priest, Human Hunter, Dwarf Shaman, Orc Mage, Troll Warlock and Undead Paladin.
Skyborne keep vanilla's asymmetry: Shaman only on Horde, Mage only on Alliance.
Skyborne speak Darnassian.
Soul Link moved from a 31-point to a 21-point talent, so it's live at level 30. Every Warlock finalist ran 21 in Demonology.
Spell, melee and ranged hit are one stat in Forever, and so is crit.
Spring 2027 brings two new raids (10 and 20 players), two new dungeons, a new zone and a legendary questline.
Stoneform now cuts physical damage taken instead of adding armor.
Taldramir's questline in the client has three stages and ties into Hyjal Summit, and it looks built for healers.
Talent trees add a 16-point milestone talent between the classic 11, 21 and 31.
Talent trees drop a lot of the boring +1% talents in favor of choices you actually feel.
The Enchanting camp item is an Enchanted Lute, and its buff stands in for Mark of the Wild.
The Forever Open grand final ended around 4:30 AM Paris time, hours past schedule.
The Mor'ladim quest in Duskwood now also offers the Ladimore Heirloom Ring for spellcasters.
The PvP ruleset uses faction balance systems similar to Season of Discovery.
The Ruins of Lordaeron, the empty courtyard above the Undercity, are a full dungeon in Forever as the Forsaken try to reclaim them.
The Skinning camp item is a Camp Chair: +2% crit, standing in for Moonkin Aura.
The beta Black Market sold a Gift of Galloping: +10% mounted speed for 15 days, for 150 gold.
The beta client holds over eight hours of music, including a remastered main theme and a new Skyborne theme.
The beta client lets you bank up to 25,000 Honor, up from 15,000 earlier in the beta.
The beta queue on day one passed 17,000 players.
The collector's edition statue, a dwarf and a bear, is a nod to Hardcore and to November 2004.
The rank track gives a tabard at Rank 1 and another at Rank 6, plus a battle standard at Rank 7.
The roadmap has a mystery 'revamped iconic raid' in summer 2027.
Tidal Charm and Whitemane's Chapeau come back reworked among hundreds of items with new effects.
Tranquil Air Totem is gone, and Fire Nova is now a spell that erupts from your fire totem.
Uncommon and rare dungeon drops unlock their look for every eligible player in the group, not just the winner.
Vampiric Embrace is on a 30-second cooldown and can't be resisted anymore.
You can enter Darkspear Islands through a portal at your faction's base: the Merchant Coast for the Horde, Northwatch for the Alliance.
You can link a profession in chat to show off every recipe you know and what it needs.
**Group up with people hunting the same mobs** → shared tags mean everyone gets credit instead of racing for kills in packed starting zones.
**Quest with friends instead of having a higher-level friend kill things for you** → quest XP isn't reduced by grouping, but kill XP is.
Undead vs a Warlock: save Will of the Forsaken for the Fear, not the first stun you see. It breaks Fear, Charm and Sleep, which is exactly what locks lean on.
Set your hearthstone at a big quest hub like the Crossroads, not your starter inn, and click every flight master you pass. Long flights only work if you've unlocked the stops in between.
**Start saving gold now, even while leveling** → 1,000g Journeyman Riding at 60 won't stall your gearing for Dec 9 raids.
**Put down a Cozy Sleeping Bag before you log out in the field** → it counts as a rested area, so you keep earning rested XP overnight.
**Capture bases first in Darkspear Islands, then run the flag to a base you hold** → steady points from the bases, plus a flag that actually scores instead of getting stuck.
**Pick Skyborne if you want a Horde Shaman with built-in mobility** → Wind Blessed haste and Walk on Air on a 90-second cooldown, on a class the Horde already loves.

**Run dungeons with people within a few levels of you** → kill XP in dungeons is 50% higher since Nov 8, and a high-level party member would cut it for everyone. Quest turn-ins stay full value either way.
entries.source: Kaivax blue post, Dungeon Enemy XP Increased - Nov 8 (via timesaver.gg server-status; Wowhead and MMO-Champion blue trackers)

entries.text: **Plan to head to Riverglades in your mid-30s** → 150+ fresh quests built for 35–45, right when the classic zones start running dry.

**Pick one surname and use it for your whole roster** → names only have to be unique as a first + last pair, so a shared "family name" is easier to claim than a rare first name, and guildies can spot your alts at a glance.

**Treat your first level 60 as an investment, even on an alt ruleset** → every 1–60 finish unlocks Legacy perks for all your alts, and Legacy is shared across Normal, PvP and Roleplay, so a Normal-ruleset character still powers up your PvP account.
**Ask a city guard for directions** → they put a mark on your map for the bank, trainers, flight master and more.
**Don't judge gear by how it looks** → transmog is opt-in, so a player in starter-looking clothes might be wearing their best gear under it.
**Drag each new spell rank onto your action bar after training** → ranks are placed by hand, so it's easy to keep casting the weaker one.
**Follow the yellow arrows on your minimap** → they point at your active quest's objective, so you spend less time searching.
**Move your abilities onto keys around WASD early** → you'll be able to move and fight at the same time. `/keybinds` shows a starting layout for your class.
**Pick up two gathering professions from level 1 (Herbalism and Mining is a classic pair)** → you sell what you pick up along the way, and that's what pays for your mount at 40.
**Queue a battleground even when your team looks outmatched** → you earn Honor win or lose, and a win only adds more on top.
**Run your first dungeons with a guildmate who knows the route** → you'll learn the pulls and the loot rules without losing a group to a wipe.
**Set aside gold for training every couple of levels** → class trainers charge for every new spell and rank, and it adds up before 40.
**Set your hearthstone at the inn closest to where you'll quest next, not where you are** → your hearth back ends your night next to tomorrow's quests.
**Skip mobs with a gold dragon on their portrait unless you're grouped** → they're elites built for groups, and they're the most common early death.
**Spend your first talent points at 10, then check a guide before you hit 20** → Forever reworked the talent trees, so a build from the original game won't carry over.
**Start setting gold aside early for level 40** → riding plus your first mount costs about 100 gold, and that's the biggest purchase you'll make while leveling.
**Stay alert at every level on the PvP ruleset** → Blizzard has no protection planned for low-level players there.
**Turn on autoloot in the game settings** → you'll stop clicking every corpse twice.
**Visit your class trainer on every even level** → new ranks and spells come every couple of levels, and missing them is the most common reason a new character feels weak.
**Ask your Engineer for a Repair Bot** → the second-tier Engineering camp item works as a repair vendor in the middle of nowhere.
**Bring a Leatherworker's Camp Tent** → its rested XP buff survives death.
**Camp somewhere out of the way on the PvP ruleset** → Blizzard warns that enemy players can find your camp.
**Camp with friends: add your item, then let them add theirs** → each character places one camp item (then waits an hour), but everyone at the camp shares every buff.
**Do "The Great Outdoors" around level 5 and learn Cooking** → that's what lets you place campfires.
**Herbalists, grow your own herbs** → the tier 2 Greenhouse grows herbs from seeds, and a Miner's Rock Garden spawns ore.

**Hunt camp blueprints in early dungeons** → in the beta, Deadmines bosses dropped the Anvil, Repair Bot and Cookie's Feast blueprints, and Lord Serpentis in Wailing Caverns dropped the Journeyman Campfire.
**Learn your profession's first camp item at skill 20** → every profession unlocks one at 20, from a trainer or a special NPC.
**Level Cooking to upgrade your campfire** → a Journeyman Campfire holds 5 camp items and an Expert Campfire holds 10.
**Melee group? Ask your Miner for a Lodestone** → in the beta client it gives melee attack power, standing in for Blessing of Might.
**No Paladin in the group? Bring a Fish Bowl** → the Fishing camp item gave +8% stats in the beta, standing in for Blessing of Kings.
**Pack Flint and Tinder and some Simple Wood** → a Basic Campfire needs only Cooking 1, holds 3 camp items and burns for about 10 to 15 minutes.
**Pick camp items your group's classes don't already cover** → camp buffs are a bit weaker than class buffs and don't stack with them.
**Place a tier 2 camp item on top of your tier 1 item** → it keeps the original buff and adds utility, like the Engineer's Repair Bot.
**Sit (/sit) at the camp for a full minute** → camp buffs only kick in after you've rested there for a minute.
**Bring gold to Powderfuse Port's Black Market** → in the beta, its reagent vendor sold Black Lotus and Arcane Crystal for a flat 50 gold.
**Budget 100 gold for riding at 40 and 1,000 at 60** → in the beta your first mount came free with training; 40 is 60% speed and 60 is 100%.
**Check the Auction House before you vendor crafting materials** → profession demand usually makes them worth more than a vendor pays.
**Hit Honored with your home faction before buying riding** → the beta took 10% off riding and your race's mounts, and Legacy Bartering took up to 10% more off mounts.
**Kill rare monsters whenever you see one** → Forever added hundreds of new rare drops and improved world-drop epics.
**Level Fishing and Cooking and sell the food** → most cooked food in Forever gives stats, and some gives bonus XP, so levelers buy it.
**Look at Bartering in the Legacy Professions tree** → it lowers vendor prices on everything you buy.
**Pick two gathering professions while leveling** → you sell what you pick up along the way, and that pays for your mount at 40.
**Playing Tauren (Horde)? Use Cultivation on every herb run** → its cooldown dropped to 15 minutes, and with Herbalism it doubles your herbs.
**Save 150 gold for a Gift of Galloping at 60** → the beta Black Market sold it: +10% mounted speed for 15 days, stacking with other bonuses.
**Sell consumables, not just raw materials** → potions, food and bandages get used up, so buyers keep coming back.
**Sell your gray items to any vendor** → it's free gold, and it clears bag space.
**Skip extra mount colors early** → each one cost 20 gold in the beta, and your first mount is already included.
**Take Reagent Economy in the Legacy Resourcefulness tree** → your class abilities stop needing vendor reagents, which adds up fast on reagent-heavy classes.
**Use an Engineer's Reagent Bot at camp** → you can buy reagents and sell loot without riding back to town.
**Aim for 15 points first** → that unlocks the first cosmetic reward, a Replica Ironforge Air Rifle toy.
**Clear Onyxia, all 13 Hyjal Summit bosses and all 8 Barrow Deeps bosses** → each is a Legacy Point once raids open Dec 9.
**Clear one dungeon from each difficulty group** → finishing a Novice, an Experienced and a Master dungeon is worth a Legacy Point each.
**Finish the Lord Valthalak dungeon set questline** → it's one of only two Adventure challenges.
**Get Exalted with the battleground reputations** → each of the four is a Legacy Point.
**Grab Talented in the Adventure tree on new alts** → your talent points start arriving before level 10.
**Level a crafting profession to 150, 225 and 300** → each milestone is a Legacy Point, and there are 18 to collect across six crafting professions.
**Level crafting professions, not gathering ones, for points** → only the six crafting professions have Legacy challenges.
**Open the Legacy System with Y** → it unlocks with your first Legacy Point, usually at level 25. Hitting 150 in a crafting profession or exploring the whole map works too.
**Pick Well Rested if you play in short sessions** → you build rested XP faster and can bank more of it.
**Pick up PvP points even as a casual** → Ranks 3 and 7 and Field of Honor weeks 4, 7 and 10 are all Legacy challenges.
**Planning to try Hardcore when it arrives? Earn some points there** → Hardcore points count on every ruleset, but points from Normal, PvP or Roleplay don't carry into Hardcore.
**Push to 55 points for the Spectral Bear mount** → the track also gives a cub pet at 25 and a tabard at 40.
**Spend Legacy Points per character** → points are shared across your account, but each character picks its own perks.
**Spend points with your main in mind** → each character can spend up to 16 points at launch across three trees: Professions, Adventure and Resourcefulness.
**Take Permanence if you camp a lot** → in the beta it made camp buffs last longer.
**Check out Shen'dralas, between Mulgore and Desolace** → it's one of Forever's new zones, with dozens of new quests.
**Check the nameplate before you pull** → a gray one means someone else tagged it first, and only they get credit.
**Eat cooked food before a long quest session** → Well Fed gives +5% kill XP for about 15 minutes, on top of camp and sleeping-bag buffs.
**Explore as you quest** → entering an area for the first time gives a little XP, and uncovering the whole map is a Legacy Point.
**Fight monsters your own level instead of easy green ones** → Blizzard cut the XP from green mobs compared to Classic, to balance the new food and camp buffs.
**Head to Riverglades in your mid-30s** → it's a brand-new zone with nearly 200 quests for both factions, plus Krol'dok Stronghold at 40–45.
**Log out in an inn, a city or on a Cozy Sleeping Bag** → you build rested XP, which doubles your kill XP until it runs out.
**Look for the Cozy Sleeping Bag questline from about level 14** → the bag counts as a rested area out in the world, and its buff survives death.
**Mix dungeon runs into your questing** → kill XP in dungeons went up 50% on Nov 8, and the dungeon quests still pay the biggest chunk of a run's XP.
entries.source: https://timesaver.gg/tools/wow-forever/server-status (Kaivax blue post, Dungeon Enemy XP Increased - Nov 8; also Wowhead/MMO-Champion blue trackers)

entries.text: **Need a break from your main? Level another class to 25** → Legacy gives a point for reaching 25, 45 and 60 on every class, and it all feeds your account.
**Pick up every dungeon quest before you zone in** → Blizzard moved most dungeon XP from kills into quest rewards.
**Plan your first Legacy Point for level 25** → that's when most players unlock the Legacy System (Y) and its account-wide perks.
**Plan your level-40 gold for two things** → your first mount and dual specialization both unlock at 40.
entries.source: Blizzard class deep dive Oct 7 via https://kami-labs.fr/en/wow-forever/wow-forever-niveau-40-monture-double-specialisation/ ; https://buyboost.com/news/wow-forever/wow-forever-dual-spec

entries.text: **Quest with friends freely** → grouping doesn't reduce the XP you get for turning in quests.
**Save rested bubbles for grinding, and quest when they run out** → rested XP doubles monster XP but does nothing for quest turn-ins.
**Skip skull mobs, and move on once things turn gray** → skulls are 5+ levels above you, and mobs or quests 5+ below you give nothing.
**Stack every XP buff at once** → rested XP, Well Fed and the sleeping bag's Well-Rested all applied together in the beta.
**Do the starting-zone profession quest** → it hands you a book for Mining, Skinning or Herbalism plus 2 free skill points.
**Engineers: sell your gadgets to everyone** → many new Engineering items shown at BlizzCon are Bind on Equip and don't need Engineering to use.
**Find the special Artisan trainer at level 35** → regular trainers stop at Expert, and Artisan takes you from 225 to 300.
**Gathering? Take Bountiful Harvest in the Legacy Professions tree** → it raises what you get from mining, herbs and skinning.
**Grab an early reagent bag** → it gets its own slot, separate from your five normal bags. Small gathering bags drop early, and Tailors can make a 6-slot Linen Reagent Bag.
**Leatherworkers: build your Tanning Rack at 125** → a Nov 6 hotfix lowered it from 140, and its skill-up range moved down to match.
**Level Cooking, First Aid and Fishing anyway** → secondary professions can't be unlearned, so there's no downside to leveling them.
**Pair your gathering and crafting professions** → Mining feeds Blacksmithing or Engineering, Herbalism feeds Alchemy, and Skinning feeds Leatherworking.
**Pick two primary professions, then add Cooking, First Aid and Fishing** → those three don't use up a primary slot.
**Playing Tauren (Horde)? Take Herbalism anyway** → Tauren can pick herbs without it, and get double herbs with it.
**Playing a Dwarf (Alliance)? Keep Find Treasure on** → it now runs alongside other tracking and can find extra items in most chests.
**Take a crafting profession to 300 for a title** → each one has a certification that unlocks a title, like Alchemist or Engineer.
**Think twice before dropping a profession** → unlearning wipes all progress, and you start over from 1.
**Track a recipe while you farm (K opens professions)** → it turns into a shopping list in your objectives.
**Train up at levels 10, 20 and 35** → Journeyman, Expert and Artisan raise your cap to 150, 225 and 300, once you have 50, 125 and 200 skill.
**Watch the colored arrows on nodes and recipes** → orange, yellow, green and gray show your skill-up chance before you spend materials.
**Aim for Rank 2 early** → that's where the PvP trinket unlocks.
**Buy the blue Honor set first, then look for Emboldened Seals** → the epic set is your blue piece plus a seal, and seals have rank requirements.
**Check the PvP tab on your character pane (C)** → it shows your rank, your Rank Points and which rewards you can buy right now.
**Do the Darkspear Islands reputation quests** → they pay Marks of Honor, and the rep vendor sells trinkets, rings, cloaks, weapons and armor.
**Do your Field of Honor journey tasks every week** → they pay Honor and Rank Points, and three per season also give a Legacy Point.
**Head to the Darkspear Raiders base at the Merchant Coast in the Barrens** → that's where you queue for Darkspear Islands.
**Hit Rank 3 for the cloaks and Rank 4 for the necklace** → they're the first gear on the rank track, well before the epic tokens start at Rank 8.
**In Darkspear Islands, carry the center flag to a base your team holds** → that's how you score. The map has four bases and the flag in the middle.
**Plan on about 10 weeks to reach Rank 14** → the weekly cap rises a step at a time, and the game files open Rank 14 in week 10.
**Play a few battlegrounds every week instead of one huge weekend** → Rank Points have a weekly cap.
**Play the battleground you actually enjoy** → Honor rates were evened out, so Alterac Valley isn't the only efficient pick anymore.
**Playing Undead (Horde)? Don't count on Will of the Forsaken against Scatter Shot** → Blizzard made it unusable while you're Scatter Shotted.
**Playing Undead (Horde)? Save Will of the Forsaken for the big one** → it breaks Fear, Charm and Sleep.
**Push your Darkspear Islands faction to Exalted** → it unlocks a short questline for that faction's tabard.
**Queue Darkspear Islands from level 30** → it's open to levels 30–60, 15 players a side, from any capital's battlemaster.
**Queue on a battleground's holiday week** → holiday-week battlegrounds give bonus Honor and Rank Points.
**Start battlegrounds at level 10** → the game files open Warsong Gulch at 10, Arathi Basin at 20 and Alterac Valley at 51.
**Tauren: don't stack Plainsrunning before the gates open** → a Nov 5 hotfix stopped it stacking in the prep phase, and picking up a flag cancels it.
**Travel in groups through contested zones on the PvP ruleset** → the other faction can attack you anywhere outside cities.
**Alliance: ride the Menethil ship via Southshore** → it now runs Menethil → Southshore → Auberdine.
**Alliance: take the new Stormwind–Auberdine ship** → it links Stormwind straight to Darkshore, so Humans and Night Elves can meet early.
**Click every flight master you pass** → long routes need the stops in between.
**Don't plan on another race's mount** → in the beta, you couldn't buy or ride one until Exalted with that race.
**Grab the Riverglades flight paths** → the beta map has Rog'mar for the Horde and Farholde Keep for the Alliance.
**Horde: know your zeppelin towers** → Orgrimmar's are outside the main gate, Undercity's are north of the city, and Grom'gol's is inside the camp.
**Make friends with a Mage or Warlock** → otherwise crossing continents means zeppelins or boats.
**Paladins and Warlocks: do your free mount quest at 40** → in the beta it gave the class mount, so you only pay for riding.
**Pick up Frequent Flier in your Legacy tree if you fly a lot** → it makes flight paths cheaper and faster.
**Playing Skyborne? Use your racial at an elemental convergence or ley line** → Skysight becomes +30% run speed (Horde) and Read Leyline +100% regen (Alliance) for an hour, through death.
**Playing Tauren (Horde)? Keep moving on foot** → Plainsrunning now builds up to +60% run speed, though it no longer speeds up your mount.
**Playing a Druid? Use Teleport: Moonglade** → it gets you out of anywhere for free, with a flight master waiting when you land.
**Playing a Shaman or Druid? Use your travel form** → you get it well before the level-40 mount.
**Skyborne: take the skyboat when you finish Zephras Isle** → it carries you to Mulgore (Horde) or Dalaran (Alliance) to join the main world.
**Take The Quick and the Dead if you die a lot** → your ghost runs faster, and your helpful spells cost nothing for a minute after you come back.
**Use the Tanaris ship to reach Riverglades** → a Steamwheedle boat runs to Powderfuse Port, a neutral goblin town both factions can use.
